page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a baseline frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the weak category, with single-threaded gzip compression registering in the bottom 10%. However, the instance leverages its 16 dedicated cores to achieve average multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with uncached large-block reads at 76.43 GB/sec and writes at 55.34 GB/sec, though the Passmark memory score itself is weak.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.4xlarge is its modest single-threaded execution speed and lack of local storage, which limits its utility for disk-heavy or single-core bound tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a high density of dedicated memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier CPU speeds. It is suitable for workloads such as Redis in-memory caching, where it achieves 11.3 million SET operations per second, medium-scale database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
